name: Cain
description: Man living at the time before the Flood

points: Video game parallel taught in class: in God of War the main character Kratos, a Spartan, is tricked by the gods into killing his wife and child, and the gods place their ashes upon his skin and turn him white. The class drew the parallel to Cain being made to match the blood he spilled. They put these hints in games here and there.
Cain did not build a metropolis for one wife and one child. There were many people around at this time, because Adam and Eve had many children, inside and outside of the Garden of Eden.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: Adam knew his wife; she conceived and bare Cain. These are the children they had when they were cast out of the garden; Cain, their firstborn that they had when they were cast out. I'm emphasizing that. And Eve said, I have gotten a man from the Lord.

Everyone that findeth me shall slay me: anybody's going to know, that's that murderer right there. How they know? He going to look different, cuz that melanin is gone. When you examine the so-called white man today, look at him: you see his blood flowing right through his skin. He's red, like the same blood that Cain shed in that ground. That's what happened to him.

And Cain knew his wife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch: and he builded a city. Obviously it was a bunch of people around at this time; Adam and Eve had children prior; that's where Cain got his wife from. Cain built the city, and that city was called Enoch.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

points: Power over resources, power over music, and power over weapons. What is that one word? Influence: power and dominance over the world. That is what Cain had back then, and that is what he has today. The righteous at this point were pretty much gone; Abel was dead, and evil began to grow and dominate the earth.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: Abel was a keeper of sheep; he was a shepherd. But Cain was a tiller of the ground. So where did Cain spend most of his time? In the field.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

points: Cain was born first; make a mental note of that, just like Esau. Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground, out working the field. Who else was a man of the field? It is already letting you know what is going on.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

points: Satan was whispering all kinds of things in Cain's head concerning his brother, and what Cain ended up doing was rising up and killing his brother. Satan was behind all of that. Satan will play with your mind.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness

points: Here is the birth of trade and of religion with Cain and Abel: Abel a keeper of sheep, Cain a tiller of the ground.

note.label: Genesis 4: Cain, Abel, and the Sons of the Wicked

points: And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord. So Cain brought fruits to offer to God.

note.label: Esau the Hater, Liar, and Killer

points: In process of time Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering: he already knew right from wrong, because his father taught him sacrifice. But in a process of time Cain got evil; he did not do what the Lord commanded.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

points: The two greatest things that destroy people in this truth are lust and bitterness. Lust is number one; from time to time you hear about brothers and sisters falling into fornication, and some never recover themselves. But bitterness is something very hard for brothers to recover from. I have seen a lot of brothers and sisters leave the truth because of bitterness. So let us go to the beginning: Cain was the first one to develop bitterness.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness

points: Cain's offering was not respected and Abel's was. It was about election, not about works, as with Jacob and Esau.
Cain was wroth and his countenance fell. The same reason Cain hated Abel is the reason Esau hates Jacob.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

points: Remember the earth was cursed in chapter 3, so it was hard to get fruit out of the ground; that is part of why Cain was angry.

note.label: Genesis 4: Cain, Abel, and the Sons of the Wicked

points: But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell. So Cain is angry at the Lord. Now, I am God, I am giving you instruction. Why would you be mad at me?

note.label: Esau the Hater, Liar, and Killer

points: And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell. Why was he upset? He understood the law and knew what God wanted. He was upset because of Abel: Abel shined a light on his darkness. Abel was the righteous, and it put a magnifying glass on Cain's disobedience. It's the same today: our light puts a magnifying glass on a lot of these false doctrines and camps that won't get right.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

points: Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell: what really got this thing started? Correction. The correction became grievous, and that grievous spirit nourished the bitterness until it grew into murder.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

points: And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell. That is where the bitterness starts. That anger came from jealousy. Anger, jealousy, malice, all these things go hand in hand, and they fall under the umbrella of hatred. Thou shalt not hate thy brother.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness

points: The Most High had respect to Abel's offering and not to Cain's, and Cain was wroth.

note.label: Genesis 4: Cain, Abel, and the Sons of the Wicked

points: And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen? If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? That is good instruction. Okay, you are messing up. Not a problem. Just do what I ask you to do and everything is going to be fine.

note.label: Esau the Hater, Liar, and Killer

points: The Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? If you do what I tell you to do, I am going to accept you the same way I accept your brother.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness

points: And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him. So Cain killed his brother instead of following God's instruction. It is the same thing today. They hate us because they are not us and they can never be us. No matter how much they try to replace us, they can create a thousand churches, create a thousand doctrines, they can never replace us, because the word is sealed, signed, delivered. We are the chosen people. We are the Israelites the Bible speaks of, and the world belongs to us, and we are going to own this land.

note.label: Esau the Hater, Liar, and Killer

points: You would think he got checked and learned. No: Cain rose up against Abel his brother and slew him. When he offered that fruit, Satan already had him; now he confirms it by murdering his brother violently.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: Cain talked with Abel his brother: hey, Abel, come talk to you for a second, man. And it came to pass, when they were in the field, that's where Cain spends his time, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

points: And Cain talked with Abel his brother. What do you think was going on in those conversations? Abel was teaching, trying to correct his brother in the process of time.

And Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him. In the process of time he allowed that wrath to accumulate and increase, and that anger became murder. When Saul tried to kill King David, that was hatred inside that manifested into actions. The Pharisees, the same thing. It's going to be the same thing today; do not be shocked. We see the buildup.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

points: Cain represents the spirit of Esau in this verse; Abel has the spirit of Jacob. Cain rose up against Abel his brother and slew him. That spirit did not start yesterday; it started in the field.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: And Cain talked with Abel his brother: this is the deception. He acted like his friend, talked with him over a period of time, and lured him out to the field. And when they were in the field, Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him. That is the spirit you are rolling in when you move with that bitter spirit; in that wrath you will slay a brother, or in that bitterness you might betray a brother.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

points: Cain rose up and slew Abel. That is the fulfilment of Genesis 3:15 and the first blood shed in the war: Cain, Satan's seed, killed our forefather.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

points: Cain talked with Abel, and in the field he rose up and slew him. He lured his brother under the guise of brotherhood, as Esau stabs Israel in the back today.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

points: When Cain talked with Abel, Abel was trying to get Cain to repent. Abel was a prophet.

note.label: Genesis 4: Cain, Abel, and the Sons of the Wicked

points: The Lord asked, where is Abel thy brother? Testing whether there was any part of Cain left that was righteous. And he said, I know not: am I my brother's keeper? Am I his babysitter? Being more disrespectful. You are going to see am I my brother's keeper in numerous places today, because Cain is back today; Cain and his babies are alive and well today, and Abel's are too.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: The Lord, knowing exactly what happened, decides to test Cain to see where his mind is, if he has a conscience: where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not. That alone is disrespectful. Am I my brother's keeper? Am I his babysitter? Now you're talking smart to the Lord.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

points: He said, am I my brother's keeper? What is Cain showing? No accountability. He kills and is like, I'm not his keeper. That's what Esau does today.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

points: The ground cried out Abel's blood, and Cain became a fugitive and vagabond. His final curse, utter destruction, was deferred to a set time.
The Lord set a mark on Cain lest any should kill him. The mark is sin, which preserves the wicked until their judgment.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

points: And Cain said unto the Lord, My punishment is greater than I can bear. Remember when Cain committed that murder and he started following Satan, he says my punishment is more than I could bear. This goes into the son of destruction.

note.label: Lucifer: The Antichrist

points: Whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold: the Lord said, no one has to touch him; don't avenge Abel's blood. I'll deal with him myself. And the Lord set a mark upon Cain: that's that curse in the ground.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

points: Now the flip side: the devil's seven. Whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. Cain was the first murderer, and the teaching is that his spirit runs through Esau: complete, unquenchable vengeance, murder and bloodshed to the epitome.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: The mark set upon Cain changed him; at the beginning Cain looked like everybody else, and the Most High marked him so that any finding him would not kill him.

note.label: Genesis 4: Cain, Abel, and the Sons of the Wicked

points: And Cain went out from the presence of the Lord, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden: write this down; that area is Babylonia. Cain built a city and called it Enoch after his son; it was later known as Unuk. Nimrod came behind him, another class, and built upon the ruins of that city, that tower, and it is the same region today: Iraq, Sumer, Shinar. The older archaeologists came to this understanding; the modern consensus view calls it unfounded, trying to wash away any biblical validation.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: And Cain went out from the presence of the Lord, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden. That's the same place the cherubims was at, that flaming sword. That's where he went. Who do you think he dealt with over there? The devil.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

points: Cain found his wife in the land of Nod; there were already people on the earth during the time of Adam.

note.label: Genesis 4: Cain, Abel, and the Sons of the Wicked

points: Cain knew his wife, and he builded a city. If Cain was the only child left, why would he need to build a city? There were thousands upon thousands of people already on the earth. He named the city after his son Enoch.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

points: Cain built a city, and you do not build a city for three people; this is more proof that the earth was peopled.
Cain called the city after the name of his son, as the wicked call their lands after their own names.

note.label: Genesis 4: Cain, Abel, and the Sons of the Wicked

points: Lamech, of Cain's line, boasted to his wives: I have slain a man to my wounding. If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold. There it is: 70 times 7 in the mouth of a murderer means complete, total, utter vengeance.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold. They did not just kill the one man that hurt Lamech; they wiped out that whole lineage. That is how Esau gets down; remember who their desire was to.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

points: Lamech knew the commandment thou shalt not kill was in force in his day; that is why he appealed to Cain's sevenfold, saying seventy and sevenfold. They knew the commandments during that time.

note.label: Genesis 4: Cain, Abel, and the Sons of the Wicked

points: Seth was appointed another seed instead of Abel. Through Seth men began to call upon the name of the Lord; they started to worship the Most High and keep the commandments, while the line of Cain went on in evil and wickedness. That is why the Most High chose the line of Seth.

note.label: Genesis 4: Cain, Abel, and the Sons of the Wicked

points: By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous; and by it he being dead yet speaketh: his righteousness speaks even though he's passed, dead, and gone.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

points: Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. Not as Cain. They are Cain, we are Abel. Cain was of that wicked one. Of the devil. The anointed cherub that covereth. And slew his brother.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another. Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous. Cain didn't kill Abel because Abel harmed him; Cain killed Abel because his righteousness revealed Cain's sin and disobedience.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

points: Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother: if you are rolling in the bitter spirit, you are moving in the spirit of Cain, of Esau, today. This is the same spirit of the scribes and Pharisees: you read about them and say they were wicked, they were following the Romans, and here you are with an evil eye toward your brother. They were bitter toward Christ and wanted to put him to death; being bitter toward your brother is the same position.
And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous: Cain was the first recorded hater in the scriptures.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

points: Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain: they hate their brothers and sisters. And ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward: money. And perished in the gainsaying of Core: they want position, they want rank, they want preeminence.

note.label: Traitors and Their Exquisite Subtlety: The Judas Iscariot Effect

cases.name: Cain
cases.charge: Bringing of the fruit of the ground when the sacrificial law required a firstling; refusing correction; and murder of his brother Abel
cases.preview: Cain was the firstborn of the house after it was put out of the garden, a tiller of the ground and a man of the field.
